shortcut_name: Treating a bipartition side as a maximum independent set
evidence: The survivor explicitly uses "bipartition via BFS"; the defeated solutions likewise build "components" and "color" counts, indicating the same camp-selection shortcut.
affordance_in_statement: The manufacturer guarantees a specific structural property of this assembly: the gears can be perfectly divided into two camps, and every engagement point connects one gear from each camp; no engagement point joins two gears in the same camp.
secondary_shortcut_name: Assuming a whole color class is sufficient for every feasible k
removal_suggestion: Do not present the bipartite structure as an explicit two-camp guarantee. Instead describe the engagement graph indirectly through the scenario and explicitly note that valid solutions may mix the two camps and can be larger than either individual camp; require determining feasibility from the actual graph.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: BFS-color the graph and use a bipartition side, or combinations of sides, as the candidate independent set instead of computing the true maximum independent set.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The gears can be perfectly divided into two camps, with every engagement point crossing between camps.

common_affordance: The explicit bipartite two-camp guarantee makes it tempting to solve the problem by selecting one color class rather than computing the actual maximum independent set.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: Its component/color-count approach assumes that selecting camp vertices provides the relevant maximum; in bipartite graphs, a maximum independent set can mix both camps and be larger than either camp.
It similarly relies on BFS bipartition sets and treats their sizes as sufficient for feasibility, missing maximum independent sets that are not a whole bipartition side.
The submission produced a runtime error; its visible implementation also follows the same color-count/component strategy, so it does not robustly compute the required maximum independent set.

recommended_edit: Add a mandatory clarification to the mutable description: "A valid sensor set is not required to equal either camp; solutions may contain vertices from both camps, and some test cases have a maximum independent set strictly larger than either camp. Feasibility must therefore be determined from the graph, not from camp sizes alone."
regression_risk: This clarification could help the already-defeated color-count solutions recognize their mistake and become correct if they implement maximum matching, but it is unlikely to restore their current submissions without substantial algorithmic changes.
